description: NIGHTDRIVE asset manifest — documents the required image files, their resolution and how the engine composites them.
targetDisplay: 1920x1080 (source plates are 1376x768 and are only ever downscaled from there)

encoding.why: 4:2:0 chroma subsampling smeared the car's edges, and the old night plates were quantised to 0.59-0.82 bits/pixel, which is what produced the blocky night sky. scripts/validate.mjs fails the build if a plate drops below 1280x720, loses 4:4:4 chroma, or falls under 1.0 bits/pixel.

scene.description: Cool blue-peach dawn light, mist in valley, pine trees, black Challenger, headlights OFF
Full daylight, clear blue sky, mountain peaks, green valley, Challenger headlights OFF
Warm amber/orange sun near horizon, dramatic shadows, rim-lit Challenger, headlights OFF
Deep blue/purple twilight, last glow on mountain peaks, Challenger with lamps lit in the plate

headlights.description: Volumetric beam cone and wet-road spill. Emitter rings dissolved so the overlay adds glow instead of a second set of lamps.

scene.description: Dark mountain road, single moon, Challenger with lamps lit in the plate
scene.derivation: Per-channel colour grade fitted to the original night plate (~1 luminance level residual), so the shared camera pose is carried over and the crossfade does not jump. The photographic moon from assets/moon.jpg is composited in place of the original 40px moon.

scene.description: Deepest night, cold blue tones, paler moon, lamps lit in the plate
scene.derivation: Same fitted grade as night, with a cooler/dimmer moon to match the deeper sky.

sourceAssets.assets/moon.jpg: 2580x2452 lunar plate, used to build the moon composited into night and midnight.

regeneration.scripts/rebuild-assets.py: Rebuilds night and midnight from the dusk master and re-encodes every plate at 4:4:4 / q95.
regeneration.scripts/build-headlights.py: Rebuilds the beam overlay for dusk, night and midnight from the original beam plate.

knownLimitations: All six plates are 1376x768. That is a true 1:1 match at 1366x768 and a slight downscale at 1080p, but a 1440p or 4K display will still be upscaling. The precise fix is six identically composed 2560x1440 masters; no external paths are referenced because those files do not exist yet.
morning/day/goldenHour use a closer, front-on camera than dusk/night/midnight. Composition is consistent within each group but the car's scale shifts across the midday→dusk boundary.

The beam overlay is a generic headlight render, positioned by a single CSS transform. It aligns well at the shipped 16:9 plates but was not authored against the car's exact lamp coordinates, so a purpose-composited beam plate per period would still be better.
Weather changes the sky not at all: the plates are fixed and the Open-Meteo data only drives the temperature/icon widget.
